beats.headline: She does not need it
beats.text: Donut stands alone on the stage in her little fake headset microphone, the charm potion already taken, and a spotlight narrows on her. My name is Princess Donut, she says. She does not take out the sheet music. She does not need it. She is singing a song her mother used to sing to her, and it is called All Eyes on Me. Backstage Britney strums the Popovs' guitar, a string missing, a sad minor strum, and Donut sings: good girl, good girl, you're a good girl, my princess.

beats.headline: All eyes on the stage
beats.text: She repeats the lyrics a few times, the same song a drunken Bea used to sing to her, moving slowly to the right of the stage, and her voice soars. The spell does exactly what its title says. Everyone in the room, hunters, crawlers and the queen among them, falls under a minor charm that fixes their attention on a subject of the caster's choice. Britney lets the last chord hang and starts a faster piece, and the spotlight re-forms on Big Tina. Everyone is affected, Carl included. Only Signet seems untouched.

beats.headline: Spoken, not sung
beats.text: Both Tigrans start screaming, and Nico tries to cover the oblivious pig's ears; it would not have mattered. Donut is casting All Eyes on Me, a spell that under normal circumstances requires a song. Her charisma is now so high that she can cast it with spoken words, and after just a few seconds of her talking, her listeners cannot keep their eyes off her. She uses it to tell Penelope and the tigers that they could all use some relationship advice.
